technical-summary: Applied the stated deployment model (local, internal, non-hostile users, multi-project shared gateway, not externally facing) to the agent-sessions hardening items. Rewrote AS101 from a caller-authorization model into project isolation and resequenced it from last (order 21) to early (order 8) as a correctness item, on the strength of a real defect found in the code: gateway queue lanes key on (profile_id, generation, config_digest) with no project dimension, so two projects with a same-named identically-configured profile share one _ProfileQueue and its concurrency semaphore and queue-max-size. Corrected my earlier AS100 finding, which wrongly characterized cross-harness visibility as a boundary leak when it is the intended behaviour. Cut AS103 from cursor tamper-evidence to cursor robustness. Reframed AS102 from security hardening to observability hygiene extending the existing CON-OPR-002 enforcement, noting its rules hold independently of threat model.
user-summary-candidate: Refocused the plan's isolation work from per-caller authorization onto project isolation, and found a real bug where two projects sharing a profile name would share one queue and its concurrency limit.

technical-summary: Corrected a misdiagnosis and produced the missing configuration taxonomy design. Cross-project lane sharing is correct behaviour, not a leak, because the underlying GPU is genuinely shared. The real defect is the inverse: lane_key() returns (profile_id, generation, config_digest) with model_id deliberately excluded, so two differently-named profiles on the same model get separate lanes with separate concurrency limits and together over-subscribe the GPU. Root cause is that the lane is keyed on configuration identity rather than contention identity, because max-concurrency lives on ExecutionProfile which is a selection, not a resource. Created AS105 defining a four-concept taxonomy (Compute Resource / Model Endpoint / Execution Lane redefined / Execution Profile losing capacity), including a resident-vs-evicting endpoint residency distinction driven by the real llama-swap deployment where three models evict each other on one GPU. Blocked AS101 on it and flagged that its project-dimension fix is wrong.
user-summary-candidate: Designed the missing compute-resource taxonomy so concurrency limits attach to the GPU that is actually shared rather than to the profile that selects it, and corrected an earlier misdiagnosis about cross-project queue sharing.

technical-summary: Folded two owner clarifications into the AS105 taxonomy design. Corrected an over-weighting of the rig: it is the AUDiaGentic CLI's own embedded llama-server and is a worked example for validating the taxonomy, not a source of the capacity model. Resolved the config-placement open question: the CLI is the management plane, so Compute Resource and Model Endpoint declarations sit at the existing user-global tier of foundation/config/layers.py's three-tier resolution, and that same namespace is what the CLI later pushes to a shared gateway service; Execution Profiles, Roles and Agent Definitions stay project-local where they already are. Flagged one configuration-accident hazard: load_layered_config merges project over user-global, so a project could silently redefine shared hardware capacity unless the resource namespace skips the project tier or rejects capacity fields there.
user-summary-candidate: Settled where shared compute-resource configuration lives (managed globally by the CLI, pushed to a shared gateway later) and corrected the design to treat the CLI's embedded server as an example rather than the model.

technical-summary: Rewrote the AS105 taxonomy around the owner's clarification that a model loaded on multiple GPUs appears under distinct server names (m27b1/m27b2) and that an execution profile should name several such instances, running on whichever frees first. Made the Model Instance the unit of capacity, carrying servable_models vs loaded_model so llama-swap style eviction is expressed without a separate residency flag, dropping that concept from the earlier draft. Replaced per-lane concurrency with free-instance dispatch: an ordered pending queue where requests carry a compatible-instance set and bind to an instance only at dispatch, making over-subscription structurally impossible and deleting max-concurrency rather than relocating it. Confirmed GPUs are shared across all projects with no project ownership, so project scope reduces to record separation plus scheduling fairness. Flagged that GatewayExecutionLaneKey largely dissolves and that its persisted public id plus the two profile capacity fields make this a versioned contract migration.
user-summary-candidate: Redesigned the execution taxonomy so a profile can run on any free instance of its model across shared GPUs, which removes the concurrency setting entirely instead of moving it.

technical-summary: Refined the AS105 taxonomy for instance concurrency > 1 and reconciled it against the shared-gateway plan. Capacity is now a counted pool declared per (instance, model) pair rather than a boolean slot, since llama-server --parallel N is the efficient case and a larger model supports fewer sequences; surfaced the drain-before-swap constraint (a swapping instance cannot change loaded model with requests in flight, which can starve the non-loaded model under steady load). Found SH08 (completed, PAUSED) already designed this admission mechanism and shipped only Slice A: contention.py exists with resource_key_for/ContentionSample/contention_summary, but the AdmissionPolicy/ResourceGateRegistry with machine-wide max_concurrent and per-project round-robin fairness was never built. SH08's resource_key_for is keyed on provider so cannot distinguish m27b1 from m27b2, and its documented endpoint:<host-fingerprint> branch was never implemented. Recorded that SH08 Slice B owns the admission gate while AS105 owns what a resource key is, and that SH11 is the natural cutover vehicle. Applied the owner's no-legacy lift-all stance. Removed a stale SH12 parallel-run hazard from AS85; SH12 is completed.
user-summary-candidate: Refined the execution taxonomy for multi-sequence instances and connected it to the existing shared-gateway resource-arbitration work rather than duplicating it.

Corrected SH10's stale pre-SH18-split module references and recorded per-slice status (CLI wiring landed, OS-signal handling/architecture-test/integration-proof slices not). technical-summary: Implemented AS82: added optional surface_id to ExecutionProfile so a profile can name which AS29 session surface it launches through. resolve_for_admission resolves the named surface via an injectable surface_resolver (defaulting to providers_api.resolve_session_surface) after building the base admission snapshot, raising the newly registered RES-EXP-004 before dispatch when the surface is unresolvable or unvalidated rather than silently falling back to the provider default. ResolvedExecutionProfile gained resolved_surface_id/resolved_surface_version fields, threaded through its schema, keeping requested vs resolved surface identity distinct. Resolution intentionally stays sole-sited at the admission boundary rather than duplicated into the agent-definition preview resolver. 12 new tests plus one existing test updated for the new field.
user-summary-candidate: Execution profiles can now name which session surface they launch through, resolved and validated once at admission time with no silent fallback if the named surface isn't actually available.

technical-summary: Built and ran the real SH16 Pi gateway Docker smoke test twice, now that SH21's diagnostic capture has landed. First run passed cleanly end to end (real llama-server install, real GGUF download, real Pi CLI dispatch through the full-isolation worker, real completed output) -- the first ever recorded clean pass. Second run failed with a real, complete diagnostic instead of the old opaque error: TO-AGW-076, the isolated worker's execution attempt ran ~185.6s against the test's own hardcoded 180s ceiling, with provisioning completing before that window starts. Root cause narrowed to timing variance under CPU-only Docker inference rather than a functional defect, since the identical path passed on the first run. Deliberately did not bump the test's timeout as a band-aid; connected this finding to SH22 (activity-renewed watchdogs) as the systemic fix and the next item in the session's build sequence, rather than picking a new arbitrary fixed number.
user-summary-candidate: Ran the Pi gateway Docker smoke test for real: it passed once and failed once with a genuine timeout under load, confirming the fixed-timeout problem SH22 is about to fix rather than a functional bug.

technical-summary: Implemented SH10 Slices B and C. Slice B: commands/gateway.py installs SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGBREAK handlers on the serving process that go straight to a forced lifecycle stop (refuse-force semantics don't apply to an OS kill signal), with a raw shutdown fallback and a distinguishing exit code if that fallback path is taken. Slice C: added the architecture-boundary regression test with module names corrected for the post-SH18 layout, confirming the no-lease/drain/process-kill-in-adapters rule already held. Attempted and then removed a real subprocess CTRL_BREAK_EVENT delivery test after diagnosing it as a console-attachment limitation of this specific test harness rather than a code defect, keeping the deterministic handler-logic unit tests instead. Slice A reconfirmed as already landed; Slice D (four integration-level lifecycle proofs) remains unstarted.
user-summary-candidate: Wired real OS shutdown signal handling into the gateway service process and added the architecture test proving CLI/MCP adapters still own no lifecycle internals.

technical-summary: Implemented SH22's core mechanism: replaced the single wall-clock child.communicate(timeout=X) hard-kill in the isolated provider worker path with an activity-verified watchdog. Added managed_process.process_cpu_time_seconds(pid) (raw GetProcessTimes/proc-stat, matching the existing process_creation_identity pattern rather than adding psutil as a new production dependency) as the real, verified activity signal. timeout_seconds becomes a grace period rather than an immediate kill; genuine CPU-consuming progress extends the wait up to a 2700s absolute safety ceiling matching the already-adopted operational policy, while a verified stall (flat CPU for 2 consecutive polls past the grace period) is still caught promptly. Confirmed the one regression risk that mattered: the existing hung-worker integration test still passes, proving a truly stuck worker is not given a 45-minute grace. Directly fixes the TO-AGW-076 false-positive class SH16's Docker smoke test hit. Recorded seven remaining SH22 steps (durable field split, richer activity sources, terminal classification set, status API exposure, profile policy, Docker e2e) as deliberately deferred, not silently dropped.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed the gateway killing real-but-slow agent work at an arbitrary timeout, by only killing workers that have genuinely stopped making progress rather than ones that have just run long.

technical-summary: Implemented SH11 Slices A-C: modeled gateway management (embedded/standalone/automatic) as exclusive component implementations using the existing foundation/features/* machinery already used by planning and coding-lsp, per RV736's correction to reuse rather than invent a second mechanism. Added the three implementation descriptors (dropping mcp-gateway per RV736 M3), a resolver in get_gateway_client() with env-override/component-config/schema-default precedence and an optional project_root parameter preserving exact backward compatibility, and generic gateway_status/list/select/get_config/set_config functions wired onto the existing ag-agents-mgmt MCP server per RV736 M2 (no new server, no implementation-specific tools). Renamed InProcessGatewayClient to EmbeddedGatewayClient with no compatibility alias. Fixed an unrelated pre-existing typo found via collection failure. Discovered and worked around a live instance of AS76's tracked registry-churn defect class in a previously-uninventoried registry (foundation/features/registry.py), confirmed to also affect the existing planning and coding-lsp components. Slices D-G (conformance matrix, soak evidence, default flip, deferred MCP gateway family) remain, explicitly recorded as not attempted.
user-summary-candidate: Gateway management (embedded/standalone/automatic) can now be switched declaratively through the same component-config mechanism other parts of the system already use, instead of only environment variables.

technical-summary: Implemented SH11 Slice D. Added the embedded coexistence guard: a read-only ownership check reusing foundation.system.managed_service_owner's exact proof primitives (observe_process/ownership_matches, not reimplemented), wired into get_gateway_client() with refuse-by-default per RV736 A6, warn as an explicit escape hatch, and env-override precedence over project config. Added a conformance matrix proving EmbeddedGatewayClient and StandaloneGatewayClient return identical canonical results for identical submit/status/cancel inputs, plus a structural protocol-method check, with automatic's conformance covered by standalone's since start_or_attach_gateway returns a StandaloneGatewayClient. Audited the item's four-entry adapter inventory: two entries (agent_jobs/control.py, event_observer.py, and 'reviewer-agent') confirmed stale via import grep and module search respectively, not force-fit into new checks; the two real consumers were already covered by an existing architecture test. 12 new tests total.
user-summary-candidate: Finished SH11 Slice D: the embedded gateway now refuses to run alongside a live shared gateway by default, and a conformance test proves switching between gateway implementations doesn't change what callers receive.

technical-summary: Reviewed AS105 before closing it: found and removed two stale duplicate sections left over from an earlier, superseded 4-concept/residency-flag draft that contradicted the final 3-concept Model-Instance-based design, and found the drain-before-swap constraint was referenced in validation/risk sections but never actually written down as a mechanism. Wrote the missing mechanism section, produced concrete implementable schema sketches for both new user-global declarations (compute-resources.yaml, model-instances.yaml), the changed ExecutionProfile shape, the rig validation case, and the dispatch queue types. Resolved the item's two remaining open sub-decisions explicitly (project-tier override closed via project_root=None; old-record cutover fails with a registered error, never silently deleted, matching this project's existing fail-closed pattern) rather than leaving them as open questions for the implementer. Closed as a completed design item -- all acceptance criteria are about deciding, not building, and are now all satisfied.
user-summary-candidate: Finished and cleaned up the compute-resource taxonomy design: removed leftover contradictory content from an earlier draft, wrote down a constraint that was referenced but never explained, and produced concrete schemas ready to implement against.

technical-summary: Implemented AS101 Slice 1: Compute Resource and Model Instance declarations at the user-global config tier, mirroring ExecutionProfile's existing model/API/validator shape exactly. Neither API accepts a project_root parameter, closing AS105's project-override hazard structurally rather than by validation. ModelInstanceStore.list_serving() is the compatible-instance-set query verified against the exact m27b1/m27b2 same-logical-model-different-GPU scenario that motivated the whole taxonomy, plus a llama-swap-style multi-model instance and AS105's rig worked example. 10 new MCP tools on the existing ag-agents-mgmt server, 23 new tests. Rewrote AS101's own plan item against AS105's finalized design and confirmed via direct grep that the ExecutionProfile.instances field and the free-instance dispatch mechanism are one atomic, inseparable change (nothing can resolve an instance set into a concrete model_id for dispatch without the dispatch mechanism existing). Deliberately deferred that correctness-critical rewrite (replacing queue.py's live admission loop that SH07's crash-recovery guarantees depend on) to its own dedicated pass rather than rushing it.
user-summary-candidate: Built the first real slice of the compute-resource taxonomy: operators can now declare GPUs and named model instances, including the exact multi-GPU scenario that motivated the whole redesign.
